summary: Inventory application deployed successfully. Node2 and node3 serve it on port 8080; node1 load-balances HTTP traffic across both on port 80. Configuration survived sequential restarts of all three nodes. RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 were preserved.
actions_performed: Installed the RHEL-supported Apache 2.4.62 package on all nodes.
Configured persistent inventory backends on node2 and node3.
Configured persistent round-robin reverse-proxy balancing on node1.
Enabled required firewall and SELinux access.
Verified direct backend responses, balanced traffic, single-backend continuity, and full-pool recovery.
Restarted node2, node3, and node1 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Inventory application on node2 and node3 port 8080
evidence.summary: Both nodes have active/enabled Apache, valid configuration, port 8080 listeners, and intact inventory content identifying the correct backend.

evidence.requirement: Node1 load-balances HTTP on port 80 across both backends
evidence.summary: Node1 listens on port 80 and repeated requests alternate between node2 and node3 before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Service continuity with one backend unavailable
evidence.summary: During node3's restart, requests continued through node2; after recovery, alternating responses from both backends resumed.
Initial and final evidence shows RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 on every node.
